edition_or_version: Draft/early published version, October 2020 presentation (not Ed. 3)
requirement_paraphrase: Slides describe a goal-based claim-argument-evidence structure; safety case must account for ODD violations; SPIs must show whether behaviour is safe, whether safety-case assumptions hold, and whether field data matches expectations; field alerts trigger root-cause fixes.

UL states the safety case must show that relevant objects are detected and classified within the intended ODD, and must show a robust mix of analysis, simulation, closed-course and safe public-road testing for the initial vehicle and each software update; no fixed road-mile number is required.
Edition 3 added requirements on post-incident behaviour; also added a more precise definition of one preferred safety performance indicator (SPI) form.

Covers building and evaluating a safety argument for vehicles operating in autonomous mode without expected human intervention; scope includes foreseeable misuse and physical attacks, excludes detailed information security.
applies_to: Autonomous vehicles/products (UL 4600 is not itself law; may be required by contract or referenced by a regulator)

requirement_paraphrase: Says its requirements are necessary but possibly not sufficient for an acceptable item safety case; prompt element lists are non-exhaustive and teams must add items relevant to the item and its operational design domain.

UNECE WP.29 adopted (24 Jun 2026, reported) a regulation for fully driverless ADS built on a safety case and safety management system; manufacturers must show no unreasonable safety risk using credible testing, including validated virtual environments, proving-ground testing and real-world trials, plus in-service monitoring/reporting and a Data Storage System for Automated Driving. (Blog does not mention ODD or SAE levels.)

Reported to require ongoing post-deployment monitoring and reporting; a Data Storage System for Automated Driving; prompt reporting of critical events (collisions, operation outside ODD, cybersecurity incidents, emergency manoeuvres, unauthorized modifications) with follow-up reports within 30 days where required; annual safety-performance data.
Reported to bar real-time in-vehicle self-learning that changes driving behaviour, and to require a software update process, remote termination capability and cybersecurity controls.

instrument: UNECE WP.29 ADS regulation (reported as GTR No. 26 / UN Regulation No. 185; doc ECE-TRANS-WP.29-2026-139e)
clause_or_section_seen: As reported by secondary sources (clause numbers not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers must reportedly submit a safety case showing the ADS presents no unreasonable risk (at least as safe as a competent and careful human driver) and maintain an audited lifecycle-wide SMS; compliance is reportedly shown via simulation, closed-track and real-world validation.
applies_to: L3-L5 ADS vehicles in jurisdictions applying the UN instrument

instrument: Vardal et al. - Learning Run-time Safety Monitors for ML Components
requirement_paraphrase: Builds a monitor from perturbation experiments (haze, blur) that predicts safety level of ML output; reports 92% monitor accuracy on a simple traffic-sign case; authors list limitations (uniform perturbations, single-shot inputs).

instrument: Willers et al., deep learning safety concerns in perception
requirement_paraphrase: Paper aims to list technical safety concerns of deep learning in perception for robots, drones and vehicles and mitigations, and to identify missing mitigations.
applies_to: Deep learning perception in autonomous agents
